html:
John I Tzimiskes was emperor of the Byzantine Empire from 969 to 976, one of the soldier-emperors of its great age of reconquest.

He came from an Armenian family of generals and fought beside his uncle Nikephoros II Phokas in the wars against the Arabs in the east. In December 969 he and the empress Theophano had Nikephoros murdered in his bedroom, and John took the throne as senior emperor beside the young Basil II and his brother. To win the church's pardon he sent Theophano into exile.

His wars:

  • In 970 and 971 he drove the Rus of Prince Sviatoslav out of Bulgaria, after the siege of Dorostolon on the Danube, and took eastern Bulgaria for the empire.
  • He held Antioch, retaken just before his reign, and in 974 and 975 raided deep into Syria and upper Mesopotamia.

He was generous to the church, and grants from him helped the Great Lavra and the other monasteries of Mount Athos. He died suddenly in 976, of illness, though some at the time said poison. Basil II then began his long reign.
sum: John I Tzimiskes was emperor of the Byzantine Empire from 969 to 976, one of the soldier-emperors of its great age of reconquest.
